ety.text: Proto-Indo-European *h₂en-der. Proto-Germanic *an Proto-West Germanic *ana Old English on Middle English on English on Proto-Indo-European *wert-der. Proto-Germanic *wardaz Old English -weard English -ward English onward From on + -ward.

ex: There was an onward rush as the gates opened.

senses.d: Advanced in a forward direction or toward an end.
ex: Within a while, Philoxenus came to see how onward the fruits were of his friend's labour.
Onward Christian soldiers, marching as to war...

senses.d: To keep going; to progress or persevere.

ex: The application has been delivered to the Nanking department of the Waichiaopu on January 19th for being kindly onwarded to Chungking.
We took the lot and patched them up before onwarding them back .

ety.text: Likely borrowed from Catalan avant (as Spanish avante was), from Late Latin ab ante (“before, in front of”).
